newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE TO FIRMER ON TUESDAY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE TO FIRMER ON TUESDAY.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted stable to firmer on Tuesday despite a cash surplus at opening, dealers said.
They said the central Reserve Bank auctioned treasury bills worth Z$485 million to mop up excess liquidity at a firmer yield of 17.11 percent from 16.64 percent on Monday.
"The sentiment in the market at the moment is that the rates should go up (in line with inflation, currently at 19.9 percent)," one dealer explained.
In the secondary market, discount houses were looking to buy treasury bills at 17.25 percent and sell them at 17.15 percent while call money added one percentage point to 17 percent.

Bankers acceptance bills were quoted unchanged at 17.25 and 17.15 percent (buying and selling respectively) while NCDs with maturity of 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at a steady 18 percent but sold at 16.75 from 17.50 percent.
Reserve Bank figures showed the market started off with a Z$178 million surplus compared with Z$58 million the previous day.
